lines.text: Do you know how a huge file gets sent over the internet? A ten gigabyte video never travels in one piece.
The internet moves data in small packets, about fifteen hundred bytes each. Your video becomes millions of them.
Each packet can take its own path through the routers, and they can arrive out of order. Your device puts them back in sequence.
If one goes missing, the receiver notices the gap, and just that packet is sent again. Nothing restarts.
To be sure nothing got corrupted, data carries a checksum: a short fingerprint. Flip a single bit, and the fingerprint no longer matches.
Big transfers go further. They split the file into large parts, and send several at once. So a dropped connection only costs one part.
Orbi does exactly that. Files up to twenty gigabytes go in parts of about thirty two megabytes, three at a time. If your connection drops, only the missing parts are sent again.
